params.body:
## Why

The pages scan counts images without alt text with `<img\b[^>]*>`, so a tag ends at the first `>`, even when that `>` sits inside a quoted value. Then it looks for `alt=["'][^"']*["']` in what is left.

On kubo.global the CyberSec page describes a keycap with the prompt `>_` drawn on it. The alt text was cut at that `>`, so the image counted as having none. That made two `TAGS_MISSING` findings (EN and NL) that nobody could find on the page: all 542 images on the 40 pages carry alt. The FR page only passed by luck, because an apostrophe (`d'une`) before the `>` happened to close the quote the old check was looking for.

## What

- `Pages::imagesWithoutAlt` now reads a tag as a sequence of attributes in which a quoted value is one whole piece, and an image counts as having alt when one of its attribute names is `alt`. All of these count: `alt`, `alt=""` (decorative), a quoted value and an unquoted one. `data-alt` does not count, and neither does `alt=` written inside another attribute's value.
- Test: `test_a_greater_than_sign_inside_an_alt_text_does_not_hide_it` covers `>` in double- and single-quoted alt, bare `alt`, unquoted `alt=logo`, and a lookalike that must still count as missing.

## Checked

- `php artisan test`: 767 passed.
- pint passes on the changed files.
params.title: Read an img tag attribute by attribute, so a > in alt text does not hide it
